title: Invertibility of the canonical restriction map on local sheaf Hom
statement: Let $(C,J)$ be a small site with pullbacks, $s:C\simeq C$ continuous in both directions, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $a:(s^{-1})^*R\simeq R$. Let $P$ be a RestrictionPresentation [def-sf-twisted-action-presentation-data] and $T$ normalized TensorComparisons [lem-sf-twisted-action-tensor-comparisons]. Write $A$ for its action-site coefficient and $U$ for underlying module restriction. For module sheaves $M,N$ over $A$, define $b_{M,N}:U\mathcal Hom_A(M,N)\to\mathcal Hom_R(UM,UN)$ by transposing $t_{M,\mathcal Hom(M,N)}^{-1}\,U(\mathrm{ev}_{M,N})$ under the sheaf tensor-Hom adjunction [def-pur-sheaf-hom], in diagrammatic order. Then $b_{M,N}$ is an isomorphism for every $M,N$. No translation Hom comparison is asserted.

source.place: section-internal-hom, lemma-internal-hom-restriction, lemma-internal-hom-adjoint-tensor; restriction half of steps 11--12 of the agent-formulated twisted action-site proof. Stacks 00W0 is motivation only.

proof.text: Apply the proved conjugate-Hom-action and equivariant-currying theorem. It constructs the invertible action on the ordinary base-site Hom and identifies equivariant Hom maps with equivariant tensor maps. Its proof uses translation equivalence, tensor naturality and the ordinary tensor-Hom adjunction, independently of any restriction Hom assertion.

The equation T.tensor_action and equivariance of evaluation show that the canonical restriction comparison b commutes with the actions, using the preceding currying criterion. Tensor naturality and the definition of b show that the image of any action-site untranspose is T.tensor.hom followed by the untranspose of the underlying restricted map composed with b.

For each action-site Q, postcomposition with b on fixed-pair maps from P.modules(Q) is injective: lift two maps by full faithfulness, untranspose them, use the preceding identity and faithfulness of underlying restriction. It is surjective: untranspose the supplied equivariant map; the currying criterion and T.tensor_action make T.tensor.hom followed by this untranspose equivariant. Lift it by full faithfulness and transpose on the action site. The preceding identity and cancellation of T.tensor prove that its restricted transpose composed with b is the supplied map. Essential surjectivity of P.modules extends bijectivity to every fixed pair. Yoneda proves b is invertible in fixed pairs, hence its underlying map is invertible. No slice theorem, pure-tensor normalization, or sheafification calculation is needed.

proof_origin.place: Formal fixed-pair argument using lemma-internal-hom-adjoint-tensor, the restriction equivalence of P and normalized tensor comparisons T. Written by D4; replaces slice normalization by the conjugate Hom action, equivariant currying, full faithfulness and Yoneda.

lean.statement:
theorem restrictionHomComparison_isIso [HasPullbacks C]
    (P : RestrictionPresentation J s R a) (T : TensorComparisons J s R a P) :
    letI := P.category
    ∀ (M N : Modules P.coefficient), IsIso (restrictionHomComparison J s R a P T M N)
